📌 नियम: Plural subject / I / You / We / They + V1; Singular (He/She/It/नाम) + V1+s/es। उदाहरण – They play cricket daily.
✖ -ing रूप बिना helping verb के अधूरा है; 'been + -ing' को has/have चाहिए; -s वाला रूप singular subject के लिए है।
N61717.expe:
✔ The subject 'The players' is plural and 'on Mondays' shows a regular/habitual action, so Simple Present takes the base form (V1) 'play' – no -s/-es with a plural subject.

📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ teaching – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। teach – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'My mother' के साथ नहीं। been teaching – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
N61787.expe:
✔ 'twice a week' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'My mother' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'teaches': "My mother teaches mathematics twice a week."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ teaching – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. teach – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'My mother'. been teaching – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

N61788.exp:
✔ 'a week ago' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'sold' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "A week ago, Rahul sold the house."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ has sold – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'a week ago' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता। sells – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will sell – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
N61788.expe:
✔ 'a week ago' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'sold' is the V2 form: "A week ago, Rahul sold the house."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ has sold – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'a week ago'. sells – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will sell – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

N61789.exp:
✔ 'at the moment' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'The boys' के साथ 'are' आएगा, अतः 'are preparing' सही है: "The boys are preparing the notes at the moment."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ prepare – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। were preparing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। is preparing – 'is' एकवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है; 'The boys' के साथ 'are' चाहिए।
N61789.expe:
✔ 'at the moment' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'The boys' takes 'are', so 'are preparing' is correct: "The boys are preparing the notes at the moment."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ prepare – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. were preparing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. is preparing – 'is' goes with a singular subject; 'The boys' needs 'are'.

N61790.exp:

N61790.expe:
✔ 'next month' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will take' is correct: "Divya will take photographs next month."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ took – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next month'. had taken – Past Perfect (had + V3); used for the earlier of two past actions. has taken – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day.

N61792.exp:

📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।

N61792.expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a book in the bag' is singular, so 'is' is used: "There is a book in the bag."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ have – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). are – used before a plural noun, but here the noun is singular. am – used only with the subject 'I'.

N61793.expe:

✖ is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Ramesh'. has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

N61802.exp:
✔ 'yesterday' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'took' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "My friends took photographs yesterday."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ take – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will take – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। have taken – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'yesterday' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता।
N61802.expe:
✔ 'yesterday' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'took' is the V2 form: "My friends took photographs yesterday."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ take – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will take – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. have taken – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'yesterday'.

N61803.exp:
✔ 'right now' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'Seema' के साथ 'is' आएगा, अतः 'is checking' सही है: "Seema is checking the answer sheets right now."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ was checking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। checks – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। are checking – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'Seema' के साथ 'is' चाहिए।
N61803.expe:
✔ 'right now' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'Seema' takes 'is', so 'is checking' is correct: "Seema is checking the answer sheets right now."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ was checking – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. checks – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. are checking – 'are' goes with plural subjects/you; 'Seema' needs 'is'.

N61804.exp:
✔ 'next Sunday' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will drive' सही है: "My brother will drive the car next Sunday."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ has driven – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। had driven – Past Perfect (had + V3); भूतकाल की दो घटनाओं में पहले वाली के लिए। drove – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'next Sunday' के साथ नहीं।
N61804.expe:
✔ 'next Sunday' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will drive' is correct: "My brother will drive the car next Sunday."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ has driven – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. had driven – Past Perfect (had + V3); used for the earlier of two past actions. drove – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next Sunday'.

N61805.exp:
✔ 'run' के रूप हैं: run – ran – run। इसका past (V2) रूप 'ran' है, जो Simple Past में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: come – came – come, become – became – become।
✖ running – present participle (V-ing), continuous tense में प्रयोग होता है। runed – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'run' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता। runs – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप।
N61805.expe:
✔ The forms of 'run' are run – ran – run. The past (V2) form is 'ran', used in Simple Past.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: come – came – come, become – became – become.
✖ running – present participle (V-ing), used in continuous tenses. runed – no such word; 'run' is irregular and does not take -ed. runs – present tense form for third-person singular.

N61806.exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'ten mangoes in the basket' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'are' आएगा: "There are ten mangoes in the basket."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है। has – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए। is – एकवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा बहुवचन है।
N61806.expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'ten mangoes in the basket' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are ten mangoes in the basket."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ am – used only with the subject 'I'. has – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are). is – used before a singular noun, but here the noun is plural.

N61807.exp:
✔ Simple Present का निषेधात्मक वाक्य: कर्ता + do/does + not + V1। 'They' के साथ 'do' आता है, इसलिए 'do not' + V1 'study': "They do not study science every Sunday."
📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ are – 'be' क्रिया, V-ing (continuous) के साथ आती है; V1 के साथ do/does चाहिए। does – केवल third-person singular कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'They' के साथ नहीं। have – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं।
N61807.expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + do/does + not + V1. 'They' takes 'do', so 'do not' + V1 'study': "They do not study science every Sunday."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ are – a 'be' verb used with V-ing (continuous); with V1 we need do/does. does – used only with third-person singular subjects, not with 'They'. have – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1.

N61808.exp:
✔ 'on Mondays' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'The boy' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'plays': "The boy plays football on Mondays."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ play – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'The boy' के साथ नहीं। been playing – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए। playing – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता।
N61808.expe:
✔ 'on Mondays' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'The boy' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'plays': "The boy plays football on Mondays."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ play – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'The boy'. been playing – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it. playing – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were.

N61809.exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('yesterday, the children ___ the windows')। अतः 'cleaned' सही है: "The day before yesterday, the children cleaned the windows."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। have cleaned – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। clean – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं।
N61809.expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('yesterday, the children ___ the windows'). So 'cleaned' is correct: "The day before yesterday, the children cleaned the windows."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. have cleaned – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. clean – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events.

N61814.exp:
✔ Simple Present का प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य: Does/Do + कर्ता + V1? 'Suresh' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'Does' + V1 'carry': "Does Suresh carry the bag every evening?"
📌 Does वाले प्रश्न में मुख्य क्रिया V1 में रहती है: 'Does he play?' ('plays' नहीं)। Do → I/we/you/they/बहुवचन; Does → he/she/it/एकवचन संज्ञा।
✖ Is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। Has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। Do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Suresh' के साथ नहीं।
N61814.expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'Suresh' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'carry': "Does Suresh carry the bag every evening?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'Suresh'.

N61816.exp:
✔ 'last night' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'drove' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "Our neighbour drove the truck last night."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।

N61816.expe:

📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ will drive – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. drives – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. has driven – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'last night'.

N61817.exp:

📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'He' के साथ नहीं।
N61863.expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + does/do + not + V1. 'He' is third-person singular, so 'does not' + V1 'make': "He does not make a kite every day."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'He'.

N61864.exp:
✔ 'twice a week' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'Usha' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'plays': "Usha plays chess twice a week."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ playing – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता। play – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Usha' के साथ नहीं। been playing – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए।
N61864.expe:
✔ 'twice a week' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'Usha' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'plays': "Usha plays chess twice a week."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ playing – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were. play – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'Usha'. been playing – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it.

N61865.exp:
✔ 'in 2019' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'watered' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "Asha watered the plants in 2019."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ waters – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं। will water – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। has watered – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'in 2019' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता।
N61865.expe:
✔ 'in 2019' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'watered' is the V2 form: "Asha watered the plants in 2019."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ waters – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time. will water – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. has watered – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'in 2019'.

N61866.exp:
✔ 'Look!' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'We' के साथ 'are' आएगा, अतः 'are finishing' सही है: "Look! We are finishing the project."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ is finishing – 'is' एकवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है; 'We' के साथ 'are' चाहिए। were finishing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। finish – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं।
N61866.expe:
✔ 'Look!' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'We' takes 'are', so 'are finishing' is correct: "Look! We are finishing the project."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ is finishing – 'is' goes with a singular subject; 'We' needs 'are'. were finishing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. finish – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now.

N61867.exp:

N61867.expe:
✔ 'next week' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will bring' is correct: "My friends will bring the files next week."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ were bringing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. brought – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next week'. have brought – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day.

N61869.exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'a house near the river' एकवचन है, इसलिए 'is' आएगा: "There is a house near the river."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ are – बहुवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा एकवचन है। am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है। have – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए।
N61869.expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'a house near the river' is singular, so 'is' is used: "There is a house near the river."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ are – used before a plural noun, but here the noun is singular. am – used only with the subject 'I'. have – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are).

N61870.exp:

N61870.expe:
✔ Simple Present question: Does/Do + subject + V1? 'our neighbour' is third-person singular, so 'Does' + V1 'read': "Does our neighbour read a novel daily?"
📌 In questions with Does, the main verb stays in V1: 'Does he play?' (not 'plays'). Do → I/we/you/they/plural; Does → he/she/it/singular noun.
✖ Has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. Do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'our neighbour'. Is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is.

N61908.exp:
✔ 'right now' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'Rakesh' के साथ 'is' आएगा, अतः 'is printing' सही है: "Rakesh is printing the books right now."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ prints – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं। are printing – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'Rakesh' के साथ 'is' चाहिए। was printing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए।
N61908.expe:
✔ 'right now' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'Rakesh' takes 'is', so 'is printing' is correct: "Rakesh is printing the books right now."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ prints – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now. are printing – 'are' goes with plural subjects/you; 'Rakesh' needs 'is'. was printing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past.

N61909.exp:
✔ 'next Sunday' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will paint' सही है: "Geeta will paint a picture next Sunday."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ was painting – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। has painted – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। painted – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'next Sunday' के साथ नहीं।
N61909.expe:
✔ 'next Sunday' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will paint' is correct: "Geeta will paint a picture next Sunday."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ was painting – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. has painted – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. painted – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next Sunday'.

N61910.exp:
✔ 'hide' के रूप हैं: hide – hid – hidden। इसका past (V2) रूप 'hid' है, जो Simple Past में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 यह irregular verb है – इसी तरह के रूप: bite – bit – bitten, ride – rode – ridden।
✖ hidden – यह V3 (past participle) है, has/have/had के साथ आता है। hides – third-person singular का वर्तमान काल रूप। hided – ऐसा कोई रूप नहीं; 'hide' irregular है, इसमें -ed नहीं लगता।
N61910.expe:
✔ The forms of 'hide' are hide – hid – hidden. The past (V2) form is 'hid', used in Simple Past.
📌 Irregular verb – similar pattern: bite – bit – bitten, ride – rode – ridden.
✖ hidden – this is V3 (past participle), used with has/have/had. hides – present tense form for third-person singular. hided – no such word; 'hide' is irregular and does not take -ed.

N61911.exp:
✔ 'There + be' वाक्यों में क्रिया बाद में आने वाली संज्ञा के अनुसार होती है। 'three mangoes in the box' बहुवचन है, इसलिए 'are' आएगा: "There are three mangoes in the box."
📌 There is + a/an/one + एकवचन संज्ञा (There is a pen); There are + बहुवचन संज्ञा / a few / some / many + बहुवचन (There are some shops)। अगणनीय संज्ञा के साथ: There is some milk।
✖ am – केवल कर्ता 'I' के साथ आता है। is – एकवचन संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जबकि यहाँ संज्ञा बहुवचन है। has – अधिकार/स्वामित्व बताता है; 'There ___' संरचना में 'be' का रूप (is/are) चाहिए।
N61911.expe:
✔ In 'There + be' sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'three mangoes in the box' is plural, so 'are' is used: "There are three mangoes in the box."
📌 There is + a/an/one + singular noun (There is a pen); There are + plural noun / a few / some / many + plural (There are some shops). For uncountable nouns: There is some milk.
✖ am – used only with the subject 'I'. is – used before a singular noun, but here the noun is plural. has – shows possession; 'There ___' structure needs a form of 'be' (is/are).

N61912.exp:
✔ Simple Present का निषेधात्मक वाक्य: कर्ता + does/do + not + V1। 'My brother' third-person singular है, इसलिए 'does not' + V1 'cook': "My brother does not cook the food every day."
📌 does/doesn't के बाद मुख्य क्रिया में -s/-es नहीं लगता: 'She does not play' ('plays' नहीं)। I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't)।
✖ is – 'be' क्रिया है; V1 के साथ Simple Present के निषेध/प्रश्न में do/does चाहिए, is नहीं। has – Present Perfect का सहायक; इसके बाद V3 आता है, V1 नहीं। do – I/we/you/they/बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'My brother' के साथ नहीं।
N61912.expe:
✔ Simple Present negative: subject + does/do + not + V1. 'My brother' is third-person singular, so 'does not' + V1 'cook': "My brother does not cook the food every day."
📌 After does/doesn't the main verb loses -s/-es: 'She does not play' (not 'plays'). I/We/You/They → do not (don't); He/She/It → does not (doesn't).
✖ is – a 'be' verb; with a base verb (V1) a Simple Present negative/question needs do/does, not is. has – auxiliary of Present Perfect; it needs V3 after it, not V1. do – used with I/we/you/they/plural subjects, not with 'My brother'.

N61913.exp:
✔ 'regularly' आदत/नियमित कार्य बताता है → Simple Present (सामान्य वर्तमान)। कर्ता 'Kishore' third-person singular है, इसलिए V1 + s/es = 'sells': "Kishore sells fresh milk regularly."
📌 नियम: He/She/It/एकवचन संज्ञा + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/बहुवचन + V1। -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o वाली क्रियाओं में -es लगता है (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries)।
✖ sell – मूल रूप (V1) I/we/you/they या बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ आता है, 'Kishore' के साथ नहीं। been selling – अधूरा रूप; 'been + V-ing' से पहले has/have/had चाहिए। selling – केवल -ing रूप बिना is/am/are/was/were के मुख्य क्रिया नहीं बन सकता।
N61913.expe:
✔ 'regularly' shows a habitual/repeated action → Simple Present. The subject 'Kishore' is third-person singular, so V1 + s/es = 'sells': "Kishore sells fresh milk regularly."
📌 Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1+s/es; I/We/You/They/plural noun + V1. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x, -o take -es (washes, teaches, goes); consonant + y → -ies (carries).
✖ sell – base form (V1) is used with I/we/you/they or plural subjects, not with 'Kishore'. been selling – incomplete; 'been + V-ing' needs has/have/had before it. selling – bare -ing form cannot be the main verb without is/am/are/was/were.

N61914.exp:
✔ 'two days ago' निश्चित भूतकाल का समय-सूचक है → Simple Past (सामान्य भूत) (कर्ता + V2)। 'carried' क्रिया का V2 रूप है: "Sunita carried heavy boxes two days ago."
📌 भूतकाल सूचक: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2। इनके साथ Present Perfect (has/have + V3) गलत है। Simple Past में सभी कर्ताओं के साथ क्रिया का एक ही रूप आता है।
✖ has carried – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'two days ago' जैसे निश्चित भूतकाल-सूचक के साथ प्रयोग नहीं होता। will carry – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। carries – Simple Present का रूप; आदत/वर्तमान तथ्य के लिए, भूतकाल के लिए नहीं।
N61914.expe:
✔ 'two days ago' is a definite past time marker → Simple Past (subject + V2). 'carried' is the V2 form: "Sunita carried heavy boxes two days ago."
📌 Past markers: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, the day before yesterday → V2. With such words Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is wrong. In Simple Past the verb form is the same for all subjects.
✖ has carried – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); cannot be used with a definite past time like 'two days ago'. will carry – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. carries – Simple Present form; used for habits/present facts, not past time.

N61915.exp:
✔ 'at this moment' बताता है कि कार्य अभी चल रहा है → Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) (is/am/are + V-ing)। कर्ता 'Rohan' के साथ 'is' आएगा, अतः 'is reading' सही है: "Rohan is reading the notice at this moment."
📌 संकेत शब्द: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment। I → am; He/She/It/एकवचन → is; We/You/They/बहुवचन → are।
✖ are reading – 'are' बहुवचन कर्ता/you के साथ आता है; 'Rohan' के साथ 'is' चाहिए। was reading – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। reads – Simple Present; आदत बताता है, अभी चल रहा कार्य नहीं।
N61915.expe:
✔ 'at this moment' shows an action happening right now → Present Continuous (is/am/are + V-ing). The subject 'Rohan' takes 'is', so 'is reading' is correct: "Rohan is reading the notice at this moment."
📌 Markers: Look!, Listen!, now, right now, at the moment, at this moment. I → am; He/She/It/singular → is; We/You/They/plural → are.
✖ are reading – 'are' goes with plural subjects/you; 'Rohan' needs 'is'. was reading – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. reads – Simple Present; shows habit, not an action in progress now.

N61916.exp:
✔ 'next month' भविष्य का समय बताता है → Simple Future (सामान्य भविष्य) (will + V1)। अतः 'will polish' सही है: "Manoj will polish the shoes next month."
📌 भविष्य सूचक: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon। 'will' के बाद हर कर्ता के साथ क्रिया का मूल रूप (V1) आता है (will go, will write)।
✖ was polishing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); भूतकाल में चल रहे कार्य के लिए। has polished – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); निश्चित समय-सूचक (yesterday/next/every day) के साथ नहीं आता। polished – Simple Past (V2); पूर्ण हो चुके भूतकालीन कार्य के लिए, 'next month' के साथ नहीं।
N61916.expe:
✔ 'next month' refers to future time → Simple Future (will + V1). So 'will polish' is correct: "Manoj will polish the shoes next month."
📌 Future markers: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon. 'Will' is followed by the base verb (V1) for every subject (will go, will write).
✖ was polishing – Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing); action in progress in the past. has polished – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); not used with a definite time like yesterday/next/every day. polished – Simple Past (V2); used for completed past actions, not 'next month'.

N61917.exp:
✔ 'since last year' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब तक जारी है → Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) (has/have + V3)। अतः 'has worked' सही है: "Ajay has worked in this office since last year."
📌 'Since' + समय-बिंदु (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + समयावधि (for two years)। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous भी आता है: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ works – Simple Present; 'since' के साथ भूत से अब तक की अवधि नहीं बता सकता। worked – Simple Past; समाप्त कार्य बताता है, अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं। is working – Present Continuous; 'since' के साथ अब तक की अवधि के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता।
N61917.expe:
✔ 'since last year' shows an action that began in the past and still continues → Present Perfect (has/have + V3). So 'has worked' is correct: "Ajay has worked in this office since last year."
📌 'Since' + point of time (since 2012, since Monday); 'for' + period of time (for two years). For a continuing activity, Present Perfect Continuous is also used: 'He has been working here since 2012.'
✖ works – Simple Present; cannot express a period from the past up to now with 'since'. worked – Simple Past; shows a finished action, not one continuing till now. is working – Present Continuous; not used with 'since' for a period up to now.

N61918.exp:
✔ 'While' भूतकाल में चल रहे लंबे कार्य को बताता है, जिसे Simple Past की छोटी घटना ('a guest arrived') ने बीच में रोका → Past Continuous (अपूर्ण भूत) (was/were + V-ing): "While Lata was cleaning the kitchen, a guest arrived."
📌 नियम: लंबा कार्य → Past Continuous; बीच में आने वाली घटना → Simple Past। I/He/She/It/एकवचन → was; We/You/They/बहुवचन → were। उदाहरण: 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has cleaned – Present Perfect; भूतकालीन उपवाक्य से मेल नहीं खाता। will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ। is cleaning – Present Continuous; दूसरा उपवाक्य भूतकाल में है, अतः भूतकाल चाहिए।
N61918.expe:
✔ 'While' marks a longer action in progress in the past, interrupted by a shorter Simple Past action ('a guest arrived') → Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): "While Lata was cleaning the kitchen, a guest arrived."
📌 Pattern: longer action → Past Continuous; interrupting action → Simple Past. I/He/She/It/singular → was; We/You/They/plural → were. E.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ has cleaned – Present Perfect; does not match a past-time clause. will clean – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time. is cleaning – Present Continuous; the other clause is in the past, so tense must be past.

N61919.exp:
✔ भूतकाल की दो घटनाएँ: जो पहले पूरी हुई उसमें Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) (had + V3), बाद वाली में Simple Past ('the teacher came')। अतः 'had driven' सही है: "Pooja had driven the car before the teacher came."
📌 'before' → पहले वाली घटना had + V3 में; 'after' वाले उपवाक्य में had + V3 आता है: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' सभी कर्ताओं के साथ आता है।
✖ has driven – Present Perfect; भूत को वर्तमान से जोड़ता है, दूसरी भूतकालीन घटना से नहीं। drives – Simple Present; भूतकालीन घटनाओं वाले वाक्य में उपयुक्त नहीं। will drive – Simple Future (will + V1); भविष्य के समय के साथ।
N61919.expe:
✔ Two past actions: the one completed first takes Past Perfect (had + V3), the later one Simple Past ('the teacher came'). So 'had driven' is correct: "Pooja had driven the car before the teacher came."
📌 'Before' → earlier action in had + V3; 'after' → had + V3 comes in the 'after' clause: 'After he had left, I arrived.' 'had' is used with all subjects.
✖ has driven – Present Perfect; links the past with the present, not with another past action. drives – Simple Present; does not fit a sentence about past events. will drive – Simple Future (will + V1); used with future time.

N61920.exp:
✔ क्रिया 'give up' के बाद हमेशा gerund (V-ing) आता है, infinitive (to + V1) नहीं। अतः 'playing' सही है: "Kavita gave up playing chess."
📌 Gerund (V-ing) लेने वाली क्रियाएँ: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep। उदाहरण: 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ played – past/past participle रूप; 'gave up' के कर्म के रूप में प्रयोग नहीं होता। play – मूल रूप (V1); 'gave up' के तुरंत बाद नहीं आ सकता। to play – to-infinitive; 'give up' के बाद infinitive नहीं आता।
N61920.expe:
✔ The verb 'give up' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not by an infinitive. So 'playing' is correct: "Kavita gave up playing chess."
📌 Verbs + gerund: avoid, enjoy, finish, give up, postpone, put off, mind, deny, practise, stop, keep. E.g. 'He enjoys reading.' / 'Stop talking.'
✖ played – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'gave up'. play – base form (V1); cannot follow 'gave up' directly. to play – to-infinitive; 'give up' does not take an infinitive.

N61921.exp:
✔ modal verb 'should' के बाद बिना 'to' का मूल रूप (bare infinitive, V1) आता है। अतः 'collect' सही है: "Harish should collect the fees."
📌 Bare infinitive इनके बाद आता है: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, तथा make/let/see/hear + object। उदाहरण: 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ to collect – to-infinitive; 'should' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता। collecting – -ing रूप; 'should' के बाद नहीं आता। collects – s-रूप; 'should' के बाद क्रिया में -s नहीं लगता।
N61921.expe:
✔ After the modal verb 'should', the bare infinitive (V1 without 'to') is used. So 'collect' is correct: "Harish should collect the fees."
📌 Bare infinitive follows: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, need not, dare not, had better, would rather, and make/let/see/hear + object. E.g. 'You must go.' / 'Let him speak.'
✖ to collect – to-infinitive; 'should' is not followed by 'to'. collecting – -ing form; cannot follow 'should'. collects – s-form; after 'should' the verb never takes -s.

N61922.exp:
✔ "She has swept the floor." में संरचना has/have + V3 – हाल ही में पूरा हुआ कार्य जिसका प्रभाव वर्तमान में है है। अतः यह Present Perfect (पूर्ण वर्तमान) है।
📌 Present Perfect के साथ just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for आते हैं, पर निश्चित भूतकाल (yesterday, last year) नहीं।
✖ Past Perfect (पूर्ण भूत) – संरचना had + V3। Present Perfect Continuous (पूर्ण-निरंतर वर्तमान) – संरचना has/have been + V-ing। Present Continuous (अपूर्ण वर्तमान) – संरचना is/am/are + V-ing।
N61922.expe:
✔ "She has swept the floor." follows the structure has/have + V3 – an action just completed whose result is relevant now. Hence it is Present Perfect.
📌 Present Perfect takes words like just, already, yet, ever, never, since/for, but not definite past time (yesterday, last year).
✖ Past Perfect – structure had + V3. Present Perfect Continuous – structure has/have been + V-ing. Present Continuous – structure is/am/are + V-ing.

N61923.exp:
✔ 'sink – sank – sunk' सही V1 – V2 – V3 क्रम है: V2 'sank' Simple Past में और V3 'sunk' has/have/had तथा passive voice में प्रयोग होता है।
📌 इसी तरह के irregular रूप: ring – rang – rung, drink – drank – drunk। Irregular verbs में V2/V3 -ed लगाकर नहीं बनते।
✖ go – went – goed – 'goed' गलत है; सही: go – went – gone। undertake – undertook – undertaked – 'undertaked' गलत है; सही: undertake – undertook – undertaken। withdraw – withdrew – withdrawed – 'withdrawed' गलत है; सही: withdraw – withdrew – withdrawn।
N61923.expe:
✔ 'sink – sank – sunk' is the correct V1 – V2 – V3 sequence: V2 'sank' is used in Simple Past and V3 'sunk' with has/have/had and in the passive voice.
📌 Similar irregular pattern: ring – rang – rung, drink – drank – drunk. Irregular verbs never form V2/V3 with -ed.

N61960.exp:

✖ to take – to-infinitive; 'avoid' does not take an infinitive. taken – past/past participle form; not used as the object of 'avoided'. take – base form (V1); cannot follow 'avoided' directly.

N61993.exp:

N61993.expe:

N61994.exp:

N61994.expe:

📌 Signal words: now, at present, at the moment, Look!, Listen!. State verbs (know, like, believe) are usually not used in continuous form.
✖ Simple Present – structure V1 / V1+s/es. Past Continuous – structure was/were + V-ing. Present Perfect – structure has/have + V3.

N61998.exp:

✖ 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'will make' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'is making' – Present Continuous → does not match the past time of the other clause.

📌 Irregular verbs में -ed नहीं लगता। V2 का प्रयोग Simple Past में और V3 का प्रयोग has/have/had तथा Passive Voice में होता है। ध्यान दें: 'run' में V1 और V3 एक जैसे हैं।
✖ swear – sworn – swore गलत – सही: swear – swore – sworn; fall – falled – fallen गलत – सही: fall – fell – fallen; steal – stolen – stole गलत – सही: steal – stole – stolen।
N62059.expe:
✔ 'run – ran – run' is the correct V1–V2–V3 (base – past – past participle) sequence of the irregular verb 'run'.
📌 Irregular verbs do not take -ed. V2 is used in Simple Past (He ran...), V3 with has/have/had and in the Passive (It has run... / had run). Note: in 'run' the V1 and V3 forms are the same.
✖ swear – sworn – swore is wrong – correct: swear – swore – sworn; fall – falled – fallen is wrong – correct: fall – fell – fallen; steal – stolen – stole is wrong – correct: steal – stole – stolen.

N62060.exp:
✔ 'Every + singular noun' के साथ हमेशा singular verb आता है: 'Every officer was given a book'।
📌 'Every boy and every girl' के साथ भी singular verb ही आता है। 'Each', 'Everyone', 'Everybody' भी singular verb लेते हैं।
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
N62060.expe:
✔ 'Every + singular noun' always takes a singular verb: 'Every officer was given a book'.
📌 Even 'Every boy and every girl' takes a singular verb. 'Each', 'Everyone', 'Everybody' also take singular verbs.
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

N62061.exp:
✔ 'since childhood' उस समय-बिंदु को दर्शाता है जहाँ से कार्य/स्थिति अब तक जारी है, अतः Present Perfect (has/have + V3) आएगा: 'My uncle has lived in Neemuch since childhood'।
📌 since + समय-बिंदु (since 2018, since Monday); for + समयावधि (for two years)। ऐसे जारी कार्य के लिए Present Perfect Continuous (has been working) भी प्रयोग होता है।
✖ 'lives' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'is living' – Present Continuous; 'lived' – V2 (Simple Past) → 'since' के साथ जारी कार्य में प्रयोग नहीं।
N62061.expe:
✔ 'since childhood' shows a point of time from which the action/state continues up to now, so Present Perfect (has/have + V3) is used: 'My uncle has lived in Neemuch since childhood'.
📌 since + point of time (since 2018, since Monday); for + period of time (for two years). Present Perfect Continuous (has been working) can also express such continuing actions.
✖ 'lives' – V1+s (Simple Present); 'is living' – Present Continuous; 'lived' – V2 (Simple Past) → not used with 'since' for a continuing action.

N62062.exp:
✔ भूतकाल में चल रहा एक लंबा कार्य किसी छोटे भूतकालिक कार्य (Simple Past) से बीच में बाधित हुआ। चल रहे कार्य के लिए Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing) आता है: 'While you were typing the letter, the power failed'।
📌 संरचना: Past Continuous + when + Simple Past, या While + Past Continuous, Simple Past। जैसे 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ 'are typing' – Present Continuous; 'will type' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'have typed' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → दूसरे clause के भूतकाल से मेल नहीं।
N62062.expe:
✔ A longer action that was in progress in the past was interrupted by a short past action (Simple Past). The longer action takes Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing): 'While you were typing the letter, the power failed'.
📌 Pattern: Past Continuous + when + Simple Past, or While + Past Continuous, Simple Past. e.g. 'I was reading when the light went out.'
✖ 'are typing' – Present Continuous; 'will type' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'have typed' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3) → does not match the past time of the other clause.

N62063.exp:

📌 संकेत-शब्द: before, after, already, by the time। जैसे 'The train had left before we reached the station.'
✖ 'will post' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'have posted' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'post' – V1 (base form) → दो भूतकालिक कार्यों में पहले वाले कार्य को नहीं दर्शाता।
N62063.expe:
✔ Of two past actions, the earlier one takes Past Perfect (had + V3) and the later one Simple Past ('the guests arrived'): 'The girls had posted the letter before the guests arrived'.
📌 Signal words: before, after, already, by the time. e.g. 'The train had left before we reached the station.' / 'After he had finished, he went home.'
✖ 'will post' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'have posted' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'post' – V1 (base form) → cannot show the earlier of two past actions.

N62064.exp:

✖ 'smoke' – V1 (base form); 'smoked' – V2 (Simple Past); 'to smoke' – to-infinitive → 'cannot/could not help' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
N62064.expe:
✔ The verb 'cannot/could not help' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not an infinitive: 'The farmer could not help smoking'.
📌 Other verbs + gerund: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, deny, consider, practise, give up, keep, can't help, look forward to.
✖ 'smoke' – V1 (base form); 'smoked' – V2 (Simple Past); 'to smoke' – to-infinitive → not used after 'cannot/could not help'.

N62065.exp:

✖ 'to breaking' – 'to + V-ing' (यहाँ गलत रूप); 'break' – V1 (base form); 'breaking' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → 'used (past habit)' के बाद 'to + V1' चाहिए।
N62065.expe:
✔ 'used to + V1' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists: 'Jyoti used to break the window in childhood'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'be/get used to + V-ing' = be accustomed to: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1.
✖ 'to breaking' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here); 'break' – V1 (base form); 'breaking' – V-ing (gerund/participle) → 'used (past habit)' needs 'to + V1'.

N62109.exp:

N62118.exp:

N62130.exp:

📌 यही नियम 'Not only…but also' और 'or' पर लागू होता है। उदाहरण: 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'has' – singular verb; 'was' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → plural subject के साथ मेल नहीं।

✖ 'has' – singular verb; 'was' – singular verb; 'is' – singular verb → does not agree with a plural subject.

N62131.expe:

📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'were polishing' – Past Continuous; 'are polishing' – Present Continuous; 'polish' – V1 (base form) → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'will read' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'had read' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will have read' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → Type-3 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
N62188.expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the manager had agreed' is in Past Perfect (had + V3), so this is a Type-3 conditional (unreal past); the main clause takes 'would have + V3': 'If the manager had agreed, Anita would have read a novel'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'will read' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'had read' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will have read' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → does not match a Type-3 if-clause.

N62189.exp:
✔ 'It is high time + subject + V2 (Simple Past)' बताता है कि कार्य का समय पहले ही हो चुका है (देर हो रही है): 'It is high time my sister solved these sums'।
📌 विकल्प: 'It is time + to-infinitive' – 'It is time to go.' 'would rather + subject' के बाद भी V2 आता है।
✖ 'will solve' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'has solved' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'solve' – V1 (base form) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
N62189.expe:
✔ 'It is high time + subject + V2 (Simple Past)' shows that the action is already overdue: 'It is high time my sister solved these sums'.
📌 Alternative: 'It is time + to-infinitive' – 'It is time to go.' Same past form after 'would rather + subject'.
✖ 'will solve' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'has solved' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'solve' – V1 (base form) → not used in this structure.

N62190.exp:
✔ 'be used to' का अर्थ है 'आदी होना/आदत पड़ जाना'; यहाँ 'to' preposition है, इसलिए gerund (V-ing) आता है: 'The girl is used to eating spicy food'।
📌 'used to + V1' से भ्रमित न हों – यह भूतकाल की आदत बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'He used to smoke'।
✖ 'to eat' – to-infinitive; 'ate' – V2 (Simple Past); 'eat' – V1 (base form) → 'be used to' के बाद प्रयोग नहीं होता।
N62190.expe:
✔ 'be used to' means 'be/become accustomed to'; here 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund (V-ing) follows: 'The girl is used to eating spicy food'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'used to + V1' = past habit no longer true: 'He used to smoke' (he smoked earlier, not now).
✖ 'to eat' – to-infinitive; 'ate' – V2 (Simple Past); 'eat' – V1 (base form) → not used after 'be used to'.

N62191.exp:
✔ 'By the time you return' भविष्य के उस समय को बताता है जिससे पहले कार्य पूरा हो चुका होगा, अतः Future Perfect (will have + V3) आएगा: 'By the time you return, the students will have collected the fees'।
📌 ध्यान दें: भविष्य के लिए 'by the time' वाले clause में Simple Present आता है ('by the time you return', न कि 'will return')।
✖ 'have collected' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'had collected' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'were collecting' – Past Continuous → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।
N62191.expe:
✔ 'By the time you return' refers to a point in the future before which the action will be complete, so Future Perfect (will have + V3) is used: 'By the time you return, the students will have collected the fees'.
📌 Note: in a 'by the time' clause about the future, Simple Present is used ('by the time you return', not 'will return'). e.g. 'By 2030, we will have built the bridge.'
✖ 'have collected' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'had collected' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'were collecting' – Past Continuous → does not show completion before a future time.

N62192.exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Rekha will have been checking the accounts for two hours by noon' में संरचना will/shall have been + V-ing है, अतः यह Future Perfect Continuous Tense है।
📌 Future Perfect Continuous का प्रयोग भविष्य के किसी समय तक कुछ अवधि से चलते रहने वाले कार्य के लिए होता है। 'for two hours' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing।
N62192.expe:
✔ 'Rekha will have been checking the accounts for two hours by noon' follows the pattern will/shall have been + V-ing, so it is in the Future Perfect Continuous tense.
📌 Future Perfect Continuous is used for action continuing for a period up to a future point. The phrase 'for two hours' is a signal.
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing.

N62193.exp:
✔ जब दो subjects 'as well as' से जुड़े हों, तो verb पहले subject ('Harish') के अनुसार आता है: 'Harish as well as the students was invited to the party'।
📌 यही नियम 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to' पर लागू होता है, जैसे 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
N62193.expe:
✔ When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('Harish'): 'Harish as well as the students was invited to the party'.
📌 Same rule for 'with, together with, along with, as well as, besides, in addition to, including', e.g. 'The captain as well as the players was praised.'
✖ 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

N62194.exp:
✔ 'since/for + समय' तथा 'and is still at it' (अभी भी जारी है) बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में शुरू होकर अब भी चल रहा है, अतः Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) आएगा: 'Kavita has been writing two poems since last night and is still at it'।
📌 since → समय-बिंदु (since morning); for → अवधि (for two days)। Stative verbs (know, like, own) के साथ Present Perfect आता है: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was writing' – Past Continuous; 'is writing' – Present Continuous; 'writes' – V1+s (Simple Present) → भूतकाल से अब तक जारी कार्य नहीं दर्शाता।
N62194.expe:
✔ 'since/for + time' together with 'and is still at it' shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing, so Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing) is used: 'Kavita has been writing two poems since last night and is still at it'.
📌 since → point of time (since morning); for → period (for two days). Stative verbs (know, like, own) take Present Perfect instead: 'I have known him for years.'
✖ 'was writing' – Past Continuous; 'is writing' – Present Continuous; 'writes' – V1+s (Simple Present) → does not show an action continuing from the past till now.

N62195.exp:
✔ If-clause 'the guests leave early' Simple Present में है, अतः यह Type-1 conditional (वास्तविक/संभव शर्त) है; main clause में 'will + V1' आएगा: 'If the guests leave early, Sita will type the notice'।
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'typed' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would type' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional); 'would have typed' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → Type-1 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
N62195.expe:
✔ The if-clause 'the guests leave early' is in Simple Present, so this is a Type-1 conditional (real/possible future); the main clause takes 'will + V1': 'If the guests leave early, Sita will type the notice'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.
✖ 'typed' – V2 (Simple Past); 'would type' – would + V1 (Type-2 conditional); 'would have typed' – would have + V3 (Type-3 conditional) → does not match a Type-1 if-clause.

N62196.exp:
✔ 'wish' द्वारा अवास्तविक/असंभव इच्छा व्यक्त करने पर past subjunctive आता है; सभी subjects के साथ 'were' प्रयोग होता है: 'Usha wishes she were a bird'।
📌 इसी प्रकार: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' भूतकाल का पछतावा: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
N62196.expe:
✔ 'wish' expressing an unreal/impossible present wish takes the past subjunctive; 'were' is used with all subjects: 'Usha wishes she were a bird'.
📌 Similar: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' Regret about the past: wish + had + V3 – 'I wish I had gone.'
✖ 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'will be' – Simple Future (will be) → not used in this structure.

✖ 'had made' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'has made' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'was making' – Past Continuous → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।

N62199.exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Anil had been painting a picture for two hours before we came' में संरचना had been + V-ing है, अतः यह Past Perfect Continuous Tense है।
📌 Past Perfect Continuous का प्रयोग किसी भूतकालिक कार्य से पहले कुछ समय से चल रहा कार्य के लिए होता है। 'for two hours' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Past Perfect = had + V3; Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing।
N62199.expe:
✔ 'Anil had been painting a picture for two hours before we came' follows the pattern had been + V-ing, so it is in the Past Perfect Continuous tense.
📌 Past Perfect Continuous is used for action continuing for a period before another past action. The phrase 'for two hours' is a signal.
✖ Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; Past Perfect = had + V3; Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing.

N62200.exp:
✔ 'Either…or / Neither…nor' में verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार आता है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject 'Anita' है, इसलिए 'was' सही है: 'Neither her sisters nor Anita was present at the meeting'।
📌 यही नियम 'Not only…but also' और 'or' पर लागू होता है। उदाहरण: 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
N62200.expe:
✔ With 'Either…or / Neither…nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject (Rule of Proximity). The nearer subject is 'Anita', so 'was' is correct: 'Neither her sisters nor Anita was present at the meeting'.
📌 Same rule for 'Not only…but also' and 'or'. Tip: put the plural subject nearer the verb, e.g. 'Neither the teacher nor the students were present.'
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

N62202.exp:

✔ The if-clause 'the manager had agreed' is in Past Perfect (had + V3), so this is a Type-3 conditional (unreal past); the main clause takes 'would have + V3': 'If the manager had agreed, Ajay would have helped the poor'.
📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.

N62203.exp:
✔ 'as if / as though' काल्पनिक स्थिति (वास्तव में वे मालिक नहीं हैं) बताने पर सभी subjects के साथ past subjunctive 'were' आता है: 'Rakesh talks as if he were the owner of this shop'।
📌 यही नियम 'wish' के बाद और 'If I were…' में लागू होता है। जैसे 'He behaves as if he were a king.'
✖ 'will be' – Simple Future (will be); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been) → इस संरचना में प्रयोग नहीं।
N62203.expe:
✔ 'as if / as though' describing an imaginary situation (they are not really the owners) takes the past subjunctive 'were' with all subjects: 'Rakesh talks as if he were the owner of this shop'.
📌 Same rule after 'wish' and in Type-2 'If I were…'. e.g. 'He behaves as if he were a king.'
✖ 'will be' – Simple Future (will be); 'is' – Simple Present of 'be'; 'has been' – Present Perfect (has/have been) → not used in this structure.

N62204.exp:
✔ 'used to + V1' भूतकाल की ऐसी आदत/स्थिति बताता है जो अब नहीं है: 'Vijay used to drive in heavy traffic when he was young'।
📌 'be/get used to + V-ing' (आदी होना) से भ्रमित न हों: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1।
✖ 'driving' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'drive' – V1 (base form); 'to driving' – 'to + V-ing' (यहाँ गलत रूप) → 'used (past habit)' के बाद 'to + V1' चाहिए।
N62204.expe:
✔ 'used to + V1' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists: 'Vijay used to drive in heavy traffic when he was young'.
📌 Do not confuse with 'be/get used to + V-ing' = be accustomed to: 'She is used to living alone.' Negative: didn't use to + V1.
✖ 'driving' – V-ing (gerund/participle); 'drive' – V1 (base form); 'to driving' – 'to + V-ing' (incorrect form here) → 'used (past habit)' needs 'to + V1'.

N62206.exp:
✔ वाक्य 'Suresh will have played chess by tomorrow' में संरचना will/shall have + V3 है, अतः यह Future Perfect Tense है।
📌 Future Perfect का प्रयोग भविष्य के किसी समय तक पूरे हो चुके कार्य (by ...) के लिए होता है। 'by tomorrow' इसका संकेत-शब्द है।
✖ Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect = had + V3; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing।
N62206.expe:
✔ 'Suresh will have played chess by tomorrow' follows the pattern will/shall have + V3, so it is in the Future Perfect tense.
📌 Future Perfect is used for action completed before a future point (by ...). The phrase 'by tomorrow' is a signal.
✖ Present Perfect = has/have + V3; Past Perfect = had + V3; Present Continuous = is/am/are + V-ing.

N62207.exp:
✔ 'Neither of the + plural noun' (दोनों में से कोई नहीं) के साथ मानक व्याकरण में singular verb आता है: 'Neither of the two children was selected'।
📌 इसी प्रकार 'Either of', 'Each of' singular verb लेते हैं। 'Neither/Either' दो के लिए; दो से अधिक के लिए 'none/any' प्रयोग होता है।
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं।
N62207.expe:
✔ 'Neither of the + plural noun' (not one of the two) takes a singular verb in standard grammar: 'Neither of the two children was selected'.
📌 Similarly 'Either of' and 'Each of' take singular verbs. 'Neither/Either' are used for two persons/things; for more than two use 'none/any'.
✖ 'have' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'were' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

N62230.exp:

📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3।
✖ 'will arrange' – Simple Future (will + V1); 'had arranged' – Past Perfect (had + V3); 'will have arranged' – Future Perfect (will have + V3) → Type-3 if-clause से मेल नहीं।
N62230.expe:

📌 Type 1: If + V1/V1+s → will + V1; Type 2: If + V2 → would + V1; Type 3: If + had + V3 → would have + V3.

N62232.exp:

N62233.exp:

✖ 'wrote' – V2 (Simple Past); 'has written' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'had written' – Past Perfect (had + V3) → भविष्य के किसी समय तक कार्य पूरा होना नहीं दर्शाता।
N62233.expe:

✖ 'wrote' – V2 (Simple Past); 'has written' – Present Perfect (has/have + V3); 'had written' – Past Perfect (had + V3) → does not show completion before a future time.

N62234.exp:

✖ 'were' – plural verb; 'are' – plural verb; 'have' – plural verb → does not agree with a singular subject.

N62245.exp:

📌 इसी नियम पर: It is time / It is about time + V2; या It is high time + for + object + to + V1 (It is high time for him to go)।

✖ B) has written (Present Perfect) — not used after 'high time'; C) will write (Simple Future) — not used after 'high time'; D) write (V1 (base form)) — not used after 'high time'

N62246.exp:

✖ A) read (V1 form) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; C) reads (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; D) to read (to + V1 (infinitive)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए
N62246.expe:

✖ A) read (V1 form) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; C) reads (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; D) to read (to + V1 (infinitive)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing

N62247.exp:

📌 By the time + present tense (return), मुख्य clause में will have + V3; By the time + past tense हो तो had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left)।
✖ A) had locked (Past Perfect) — future completion नहीं बताता; B) was locking (Past Continuous) — future completion नहीं बताता; D) has locked (Present Perfect) — future completion नहीं बताता
N62247.expe:

📌 By the time + present (return) → will have + V3 in the main clause; By the time + past → had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left).
✖ A) had locked (Past Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point; B) was locking (Past Continuous) — does not show completion before a future point; D) has locked (Present Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point

N62248.exp:

📌 Perfect Continuous tenses के साथ प्रायः for (अवधि) / since (आरंभ-बिंदु) आता है; Future Perfect के साथ by + future time।
✖ A) Past Perfect = had + V3; B) Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; C) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing
N62248.expe:

📌 Perfect Continuous tenses usually take for (duration) / since (starting point); Future Perfect usually takes by + future time.
✖ A) Past Perfect = had + V3; B) Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing; C) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing

N62249.exp:
✔ Neither…nor / Either…or में verb निकटतम (दूसरे) subject के अनुसार होती है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject ‘Seema’ एकवचन है, और ‘at the meeting’ से past है — अतः ‘was’।
📌 उदाहरण: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame। सुझाव: plural subject को nor के बाद रखें।
✖ B) were (plural verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं; C) are (plural verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं; D) have (plural verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं
N62249.expe:
✔ With Neither…nor / Either…or, the verb agrees with the nearer (second) subject (rule of proximity). Here ‘Seema’ is singular, and the context is past — so ‘was’.
📌 Examples: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame. Tip: place the plural subject after nor.
✖ B) were (plural verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; C) are (plural verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; D) have (plural verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense

📌 since + समय-बिंदु (since Monday, since 9 o'clock); for + अवधि (for two hours)। Singular subject → has been, plural/I/you → have been।
✖ A) was drawing (Past Continuous) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता; C) draws (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता; D) is drawing (Present Continuous) — since/for वाली जारी क्रिया नहीं बताता
N62250.expe:
✔ ‘since/for … and is still at it’ means the action began in the past and is still going on → Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing): “Deepak has been drawing a picture since Monday and is still at it.”
📌 since + point of time (since Monday, since 9 o'clock); for + period (for two hours). Singular subject → has been; plural/I/you → have been.
✖ A) was drawing (Past Continuous) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for; C) draws (V1 + s (Simple Present)) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for; D) is drawing (Present Continuous) — cannot show an ongoing action with since/for

N62251.exp:

📌 Zero: If + present, present; First: If + present, will + V1; Second: If + V2/were, would + V1; Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3। If-clause में will/would नहीं आता।
✖ A) had posted (Past Perfect) — Third Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं; B) will have posted (Future Perfect) — Third Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं; D) will post (Simple Future) — Third Conditional के pattern से मेल नहीं
N62251.expe:
✔ ‘If the shop had been open’ is a Third Conditional: If + had + V3, … would have + V3 (unreal past). Hence “If the shop had been open, Sita would have posted the letter.”
📌 Zero: If + present, present; First: If + present, will + V1; Second: If + V2/were, would + V1; Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3. No will/would in the if-clause.
✖ A) had posted (Past Perfect) — does not match the Third Conditional pattern; B) will have posted (Future Perfect) — does not match the Third Conditional pattern; D) will post (Simple Future) — does not match the Third Conditional pattern

N62252.exp:
✔ ‘wish’ के बाद अवास्तविक/काल्पनिक स्थिति के लिए subjunctive ‘were’ आता है — सभी subjects के साथ (I/he/they were): “The players wish they were birds.”
📌 इसी नियम पर: If I were you…; He behaves as though he were a king; I wish I were rich। past की इच्छा: wish + had + V3 (I wish I had gone)।
✖ A) will be (Simple Future) — unreal स्थिति में were चाहिए; B) are (plural verb) — unreal स्थिति में were चाहिए; C) have been (Present Perfect) — unreal स्थिति में were चाहिए
N62252.expe:
✔ After ‘wish’, an unreal or imaginary situation takes the subjunctive ‘were’ with every subject (I/he/they were): “The players wish they were birds.”
📌 Same rule: If I were you…; He behaves as though he were a king; I wish I were rich. Past regret: wish + had + V3 (I wish I had gone).
✖ A) will be (Simple Future) — unreal situation needs ‘were’; B) are (plural verb) — unreal situation needs ‘were’; C) have been (Present Perfect) — unreal situation needs ‘were’

N62253.exp:

✖ B) speak (V1 (base form)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; C) spoke (V2 / Simple Past) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए; D) to speak (to + V1 (infinitive)) — preposition ‘to’ के बाद V-ing चाहिए
N62253.expe:

📌 Contrast: used to + V1 = past habit (He used to smoke); be used to + V-ing = accustomed (He is used to smoking). Likewise look forward to / object to + V-ing.
✖ B) speak (V1 (base form)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; C) spoke (V2 / Simple Past) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing; D) to speak (to + V1 (infinitive)) — the preposition ‘to’ needs V-ing

N62254.exp:

📌 By the time + present tense (return), मुख्य clause में will have + V3; By the time + past tense हो तो had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left)।
✖ A) was sending (Past Continuous) — future completion नहीं बताता; C) has sent (Present Perfect) — future completion नहीं बताता; D) had sent (Past Perfect) — future completion नहीं बताता
N62254.expe:
✔ ‘By 2030’ marks a future point; an action completed before it takes the Future Perfect (will have + V3): “By 2030, my sister will have sent a parcel.”
📌 By the time + present (return) → will have + V3 in the main clause; By the time + past → had + V3 (By the time we came, he had left).
✖ A) was sending (Past Continuous) — does not show completion before a future point; C) has sent (Present Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point; D) had sent (Past Perfect) — does not show completion before a future point

N62255.exp:
✔ वाक्य “Kishore had sent the invitations before we came.” में संरचना had + V3 है, अतः यह Past Perfect tense है — दो past घटनाओं में पहले पूरी हुई घटना।
📌 Perfect Continuous tenses के साथ प्रायः for (अवधि) / since (आरंभ-बिंदु) आता है; Future Perfect के साथ by + future time।
✖ A) Present Perfect = has/have + V3; B) Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; D) Simple Past = V2
N62255.expe:
✔ The sentence “Kishore had sent the invitations before we came.” uses the structure had + V3, so it is in the Past Perfect tense — the earlier of two completed past actions.
📌 Perfect Continuous tenses usually take for (duration) / since (starting point); Future Perfect usually takes by + future time.
✖ A) Present Perfect = has/have + V3; B) Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing; D) Simple Past = V2

N62256.exp:
✔ Neither…nor / Either…or में verb निकटतम (दूसरे) subject के अनुसार होती है (Rule of Proximity)। यहाँ निकटतम subject ‘her parents’ बहुवचन है, और ‘at the meeting’ से past है — अतः ‘were’।
📌 उदाहरण: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame। सुझाव: plural subject को nor के बाद रखें।
✖ A) is (singular verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं; B) has (singular verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं; C) was (singular verb) — निकटतम subject/काल से मेल नहीं
N62256.expe:
✔ With Neither…nor / Either…or, the verb agrees with the nearer (second) subject (rule of proximity). Here ‘her parents’ is plural, and the context is past — so ‘were’.
📌 Examples: Neither the teacher nor the students were present; Either the boys or Ram is to blame. Tip: place the plural subject after nor.
✖ A) is (singular verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; B) has (singular verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense; C) was (singular verb) — does not agree with the nearer subject/tense

N62262.expe:

📌 Perfect Continuous tenses usually take for (duration) / since (starting point); Future Perfect usually takes by + future time.
✖ A) Present Perfect Continuous = has/have been + V-ing; C) Past Perfect = had + V3; D) Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing

✖ A) have (plural verb) — singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं; B) are (plural verb) — singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं; D) were (plural verb) — singular subject के साथ मेल नहीं

📌 Examples: The captain, as well as the players, was praised; The teacher with his students is coming.
✖ A) have (plural verb) — does not agree with a singular subject; B) are (plural verb) — does not agree with a singular subject; D) were (plural verb) — does not agree with a singular subject

N62349.exp:
✔ “Jyoti did not draw a map the day before yesterday.” — did not + V1 — सही। बाकी तीनों वाक्यों में tense/verb की त्रुटि है।
📌 मुख्य नियम: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 के साथ Simple Past (Present Perfect नहीं); before + past घटना से पहले had + V3; If-clause में would नहीं; It is high time + V2।
✖ B) past घटना से पहले का कार्य Past Perfect में: has sent → had sent; C) If-clause में would have नहीं, had + V3 चाहिए (had tried); D) avoid के बाद gerund: avoided asking
N62349.expe:
✔ “Jyoti did not draw a map the day before yesterday.” — ‘did not’ + V1 — correct. The other three sentences contain tense/verb errors.
📌 Key rules: did not + V1; yesterday/ago/last/in 2019 take Simple Past (not Present Perfect); action before a past event → had + V3; no ‘would’ in the if-clause; It is high time + V2.
✖ B) an action before another past event needs the Past Perfect: has sent → had sent; C) the if-clause needs had + V3 (had tried), not would have; D) ‘avoid’ takes a gerund: avoided asking

N62350.exp:
✔ Second Conditional (वर्तमान की अवास्तविक स्थिति — वह manager नहीं है): If + subject + were, … would + V1। सभी subjects के साथ ‘were’: “If Ajay were the manager, he would solve the puzzle at once.”
📌 उदाहरण: If I were a bird, I would fly। Third Conditional: If he had been the manager, he would have + V3।
✖ A) had been, will solve — had been के साथ would have + V3 चाहिए, will नहीं; C) is, would solve — is (First Conditional) के साथ would नहीं, will आता; D) were, will solve — were के साथ will नहीं, would चाहिए
N62350.expe:

📌 Example: If I were a bird, I would fly. Third Conditional: If he had been the manager, he would have + V3.

N62352.exp:

N62353.expe:

N62356.exp:

N62356.expe:

✖ A) did, then — ‘did’ and ‘then’ are a wrong pairing; B) has, than — ‘than’ pairs with No sooner; C) had, than — ‘than’ pairs with No sooner

📌 नियम याद रखें: (1) yesterday/last/ago जैसे निश्चित बीते समय के साथ present perfect नहीं, simple past; (2) did/does/do + V1; (3) It is high time + V2; (4) If-clause में would नहीं।
✖ (A) Present perfect (has + V3) के साथ बीता हुआ निश्चित समय (last/ago/before ... came) नहीं आता — simple past ("cleaned") या past perfect होना चाहिए। (C) "It is high time + subject" के बाद past simple (V2) आता है — "wrote" होना चाहिए, "writes" नहीं। (D) If-clause में "would have" नहीं आता — "If ... had tried" होना चाहिए।
N62514.expe:
✔ "Ramesh had typed the letter before it got dark." — Past perfect (had + V3) for the earlier action, with "before + simple past" — correct.
📌 Remember: (1) definite past time (yesterday/last/ago) takes simple past, not present perfect; (2) did/does/do + V1; (3) It is high time + V2; (4) no "would" in the if-clause.
✖ (A) Present perfect (has + V3) cannot take a definite past time (last/ago/before ... came) — use simple past ("cleaned") or past perfect. (C) "It is high time + subject" takes the past simple (V2) — it should be "wrote", not "writes". (D) "would have" cannot be used in the if-clause — it should be "If ... had tried".

N62515.exp:
✔ Third conditional (बीते समय की काल्पनिक शर्त): If + had + V3 (had had), would have + V3। सही वाक्य: If Ramesh had had more time, he would have written an essay. — अर्थ: उसके पास अधिक समय नहीं था।
📌 Conditionals: First — If + V1, will + V1; Second — If + V2/were, would + V1; Third — If + had + V3, would have + V3।
✖ "had had, will write" — "had had" के साथ "will" नहीं, "would have + V3" आता है। "would have, would write" — If-clause में "would have" नहीं आता। "had, would have written" — "had" (simple past) second conditional का रूप है; बीते समय की शर्त (would have + V3) के लिए "had had" चाहिए।
N62515.expe:
✔ Third conditional (unreal past condition): If + had + V3 (had had), would have + V3. Correct: If Ramesh had had more time, he would have written an essay. — meaning she/he did not have more time.
📌 Conditionals: First — If + V1, will + V1; Second — If + V2/were, would + V1; Third — If + had + V3, would have + V3.
✖ "had had, will write" — "had had" is not followed by "will" but by "would have + V3". "would have, would write" — "would have" cannot be used in the if-clause. "had, would have written" — "had" (simple past) belongs to the second conditional; a past condition with "would have + V3" needs "had had".
