✖ (A) Past perfect (had + V3) पहले हुए काम के लिए, "before + simple past" के साथ — सही। (B) "It is high time + subject + V2 (cooked)" — सही संरचना। (C) Third conditional: If + had + V3, would have + V3 — सही।
N62516.expe:
✔ The question asks for the incorrect sentence. "Neha did not collected stamps last week." — "did not" takes V1 — it should be "did not collect", not "collected".
📌 Remember: (1) definite past time (yesterday/last/ago) takes simple past, not present perfect; (2) did/does/do + V1; (3) It is high time + V2; (4) no "would" in the if-clause.
✖ (A) Past perfect (had + V3) for the earlier action, with "before + simple past" — correct. (B) "It is high time + subject + V2 (cooked)" — correct structure. (C) Third conditional: If + had + V3, would have + V3 — correct.

N62517.exp:
✔ "actor" (ऐक्टर) vowel sound से शुरू होता है, इसलिए "an" लगेगा: Divya wants to become an actor. "wants to become" के बाद पेशा/पद (profession) बताने वाले singular countable noun से पहले a/an आता है।
📌 नियम: a/an का चुनाव अक्षर (letter) से नहीं, उच्चारण की पहली ध्वनि (sound) से होता है — vowel sound से पहले "an"। उदाहरण: an apple, an umbrella, an hour।
✖ "the" किसी निश्चित/पहले से ज्ञात वस्तु या व्यक्ति के लिए है; यहाँ अनिश्चित (कोई एक) की बात है। "a" consonant sound से पहले आता है — "actor" vowel sound से शुरू है। Singular countable noun अकेला नहीं आता — article ज़रूरी है।
N62517.expe:
✔ "actor" begins with the vowel sound /æ/ ("ac-"), so "an" is used: Divya wants to become an actor. After "wants to become", a profession/post is a singular countable noun, so it takes a/an.
📌 Rule: a/an depends on the first SOUND, not the letter — "an" before a vowel sound. Examples: an apple, an umbrella, an hour.
✖ "the" marks something specific/already known; here the noun is indefinite (any one). "a" is used before a consonant sound — "actor" begins with a vowel sound. A singular countable noun cannot stand without an article here.

N62518.exp:
✔ दिनों (days) के नाम से पहले "on" लगता है। सही वाक्य: Meena will meet us on Tuesday.
📌 समय के preposition: at + घड़ी का समय (at 5 o'clock), on + दिन/तारीख (on Monday, on 15 August), in + महीना/वर्ष/ऋतु (in May, in 2020)।
✖ "in" महीना/वर्ष/दिन के भाग या किसी चीज़ के अंदर के लिए (in May, in the room)। "since" किसी समय-बिंदु से (perfect tense के साथ): since 2010। "at" निश्चित समय/बिंदु-स्थान के लिए (at 5 pm, at the gate)।
N62518.expe:
✔ Days of the week take "on". Correct sentence: Meena will meet us on Tuesday.
📌 Prepositions of time: at + clock time (at 5 o'clock), on + day/date (on Monday, on 15 August), in + month/year/season (in May, in 2020).
✖ "in" is for months/years/parts of the day or inside something (in May, in the room). "since" marks a starting point of time, with perfect tenses: since 2010. "at" is for an exact time or point (at 5 pm, at the gate).

N62519.exp:
✔ "if" शर्त (condition) बताता है — "अगर उसे बुलाया जाएगा तो वह आएगी/आएगा"। First conditional: if + simple present, will + V1। सही वाक्य: The boy will come if he is invited.
📌 If-clause में future (will) नहीं आता: "if she is invited" सही, "if she will be invited" गलत।
✖ "lest" = ऐसा न हो कि (lest + should): Work hard lest you should fail। "whereas" दो बातों में विरोधाभासी तुलना करता है। "though" = यद्यपि (विरोध/concession)।
N62519.expe:
✔ "if" introduces a condition — "she/he will come on the condition of being invited". First conditional: if + simple present, will + V1. Correct sentence: The boy will come if he is invited.
📌 The if-clause does not take "will": "if she is invited" is correct, not "if she will be invited".
✖ "lest" means "for fear that" (lest + should): Work hard lest you should fail. "whereas" contrasts two facts. "though" means "in spite of the fact that" (concession).

N62520.exp:

✖ "A" अनिश्चित (कोई एक) वस्तु के लिए है; unique वस्तु के साथ नहीं लगता। Unique object के साथ article छोड़ना गलत है। "An" अनिश्चित (कोई एक) वस्तु के लिए है; unique वस्तु के साथ नहीं लगता।
N62520.expe:
✔ "sun" is unique — there is only one — so "The" is used. Correct sentence: The sun sets in the west.
📌 Unique objects take "the": the sun, the moon, the earth, the sky, the sea, the world. Directions too: in the east, in the west.
✖ "A" marks an indefinite (any one) thing; it is not used with a unique object. Leaving out the article is wrong with a unique object. "An" marks an indefinite (any one) thing; it is not used with a unique object.

N62521.exp:

📌 Comparative + than: better than, more beautiful than। पर superior, inferior, senior, junior, prefer के साथ "to": senior to me।
✖ "as" समानता की तुलना (as ... as) या "क्योंकि" अर्थ में। "then" समय-सूचक adverb (तब/फिर) है, तुलना का शब्द नहीं। "to" दिशा/गंतव्य के लिए (go to school; kind to)।
N62521.expe:
✔ A comparative (taller) is followed by "than". Correct sentence: Pooja is taller than Rekha.
📌 Comparative + than: better than, more beautiful than. But superior, inferior, senior, junior, prefer take "to": senior to me.
✖ "as" is used in equal comparison (as ... as) or meaning "because". "then" is an adverb of time (after that), not a comparison word. "to" shows direction/destination (go to school; kind to).

N62522.exp:
✔ "unique" अक्षर vowel से शुरू होता है, पर उच्चारण "यूनीक" consonant sound "य" (/j/) से है, इसलिए "a" लगेगा: I have never seen such a unique idea. "such + a/an + (adjective) + singular countable noun" — जैसे such a good boy, such an honest man।
📌 u/eu से शुरू होने वाले जिन शब्दों का उच्चारण "यू" (y consonant sound) से होता है, उनसे पहले "a": a university, a uniform, a European, a ewe। पर an umbrella, an uncle (vowel sound)।
✖ "the" किसी निश्चित/पहले से ज्ञात वस्तु या व्यक्ति के लिए है; यहाँ अनिश्चित (कोई एक) की बात है। Singular countable noun अकेला नहीं आता — article ज़रूरी है। "an" vowel sound से पहले आता है — "unique" का उच्चारण consonant sound से है।
N62522.expe:
✔ Though "unique" starts with a vowel letter, it is pronounced "yoo-neek", beginning with the consonant sound /j/, so "a" is used: I have never seen such a unique idea. Pattern: "such + a/an + (adjective) + singular countable noun" — e.g. such a good boy, such an honest man.
📌 Words beginning with u/eu pronounced "yoo" start with the consonant sound /j/, so they take "a": a university, a uniform, a European, a ewe. But an umbrella, an uncle (vowel sound).
✖ "the" marks something specific/already known; here the noun is indefinite (any one). A singular countable noun cannot stand without an article here. "an" is used before a vowel sound — "unique" begins with a consonant sound.

N62523.exp:
✔ "ready for + noun" — किसी काम/चीज़ के लिए तैयार। सही वाक्य: The farmer is ready for the journey.
📌 पर क्रिया (verb) हो तो "ready to + V1": ready to go, ready to help।
✖ "of" संबंध/अंश के लिए (a cup of tea; fond of, proud of)। "to" दिशा/गंतव्य के लिए (go to school; kind to)। "on" दिन/तारीख या सतह के लिए (on Monday, on the table)।
N62523.expe:
✔ "ready for + noun" — prepared for something. Correct sentence: The farmer is ready for the journey.
📌 But with a verb use "ready to + V1": ready to go, ready to help.
✖ "of" shows relation/part (a cup of tea; fond of, proud of). "to" shows direction/destination (go to school; kind to). "on" is for days/dates or a surface (on Monday, on the table).

N62524.exp:
✔ "so" परिणाम (result) बताता है — पहला वाक्य कारण, दूसरा उसका परिणाम। सही वाक्य: Nisha was ill, so she did not go to school.
📌 "so" (परिणाम) और "because" (कारण) उलटे क्रम में आते हैं: She was ill, so she stayed home = She stayed home because she was ill।
✖ "or" विकल्प (choice) या "वरना" के अर्थ में आता है। "because" कारण (reason) बताता है। "but" विरोध (contrast) बताता है।
N62524.expe:
✔ "so" introduces a result — the first clause is the cause, the second its result. Correct sentence: Nisha was ill, so she did not go to school.
📌 "so" (result) and "because" (reason) work in opposite order: She was ill, so she stayed home = She stayed home because she was ill.
✖ "or" shows a choice, or means "otherwise". "because" introduces a reason. "but" shows contrast.

✖ "by" shows means/agent or a deadline (by bus, by Monday). "on" is for days/dates or a surface (on Monday, on the table). "at" is for an exact time or point (at 5 pm, at the gate).

N62552.exp:
✔ "at night" निश्चित मुहावरा (fixed expression) है — रात के लिए "at" लगता है। सही वाक्य: Anita likes to read at night.
📌 तुलना करें: in the morning, in the evening, पर at night, at noon, at midnight।
✖ "on" दिन/तारीख या सतह के लिए (on Monday, on the table)। "in" महीना/वर्ष/दिन के भाग या किसी चीज़ के अंदर के लिए (in May, in the room)। "for" उद्देश्य या अवधि के लिए (for you, for two hours)।
N62552.expe:
✔ "at night" is a fixed expression — "at" is used with night. Correct sentence: Anita likes to read at night.
📌 Compare: in the morning, in the evening, but at night, at noon, at midnight.
✖ "on" is for days/dates or a surface (on Monday, on the table). "in" is for months/years/parts of the day or inside something (in May, in the room). "for" shows purpose or duration (for you, for two hours).

N62553.exp:
✔ "but" विरोध (contrast) बताता है — दूसरा भाग पहले भाग से अपेक्षित बात के उलट है। सही वाक्य: Pooja is rich, but she is not proud.
📌 विरोध के अन्य connectors: yet, still, however, although (although के साथ "but" नहीं लगाते)।
✖ "so" परिणाम (result) बताता है। "or" विकल्प (choice) या "वरना" के अर्थ में आता है। "because" कारण (reason) बताता है।
N62553.expe:
✔ "but" shows contrast — the second clause is contrary to what the first leads us to expect. Correct sentence: Pooja is rich, but she is not proud.
📌 Other contrast connectors: yet, still, however, although (never use "but" together with "although").
✖ "so" introduces a result. "or" shows a choice, or means "otherwise". "because" introduces a reason.

N62554.exp:
✔ "sun" संसार में एक ही है (unique object), इसलिए "The" लगेगा। सही वाक्य: The sun rises in the east.
📌 Unique objects के साथ "the": the sun, the moon, the earth, the sky, the sea, the world। ध्यान दें — दिशाएँ भी: in the east, in the west।
✖ "A" अनिश्चित (कोई एक) वस्तु के लिए है; unique वस्तु के साथ नहीं लगता। Unique object के साथ article छोड़ना गलत है। "An" अनिश्चित (कोई एक) वस्तु के लिए है; unique वस्तु के साथ नहीं लगता।
N62554.expe:
✔ "sun" is unique — there is only one — so "The" is used. Correct sentence: The sun rises in the east.
📌 Unique objects take "the": the sun, the moon, the earth, the sky, the sea, the world. Directions too: in the east, in the west.
✖ "A" marks an indefinite (any one) thing; it is not used with a unique object. Leaving out the article is wrong with a unique object. "An" marks an indefinite (any one) thing; it is not used with a unique object.

N62556.exp:

📌 पर क्रिया (verb) हो तो "ready to + V1": ready to go, ready to help।
✖ "to" दिशा/गंतव्य के लिए (go to school; kind to)। "on" दिन/तारीख या सतह के लिए (on Monday, on the table)। "of" संबंध/अंश के लिए (a cup of tea; fond of, proud of)।

✔ "ready for + noun" — prepared for something. Correct sentence: My father is ready for the journey.
📌 But with a verb use "ready to + V1": ready to go, ready to help.

N62557.exp:

📌 "so" (परिणाम) और "because" (कारण) उलटे क्रम में आते हैं: She was ill, so she stayed home = She stayed home because she was ill।
✖ "because" कारण (reason) बताता है। "or" विकल्प (choice) या "वरना" के अर्थ में आता है। "but" विरोध (contrast) बताता है।
N62557.expe:
✔ "so" introduces a result — the first clause is the cause, the second its result. Correct sentence: Neha was ill, so she did not go to school.
📌 "so" (result) and "because" (reason) work in opposite order: She was ill, so she stayed home = She stayed home because she was ill.
✖ "because" introduces a reason. "or" shows a choice, or means "otherwise". "but" shows contrast.

N62566.exp:

📌 Although/Though के साथ main clause में "but" नहीं आता; "yet" आ सकता है। noun के साथ "in spite of/despite": in spite of being tired।
✖ "Unless" = यदि नहीं (if not)। "So" परिणाम बताता है; वाक्य के आरंभ में इस संरचना में नहीं बैठता। "Because" कारण बताता है, विरोध नहीं।
N62566.expe:
✔ "Although" shows concession — working in spite of being tired/old. Correct sentence: Although Gopal was tired, he kept working.
📌 With although/though, do not add "but" in the main clause ("yet" is allowed). Before a noun use "in spite of/despite": in spite of being tired.
✖ "Unless" means "if not". "So" shows result; it does not fit at the start of this structure. "Because" gives a reason, not contrast.

📌 इसी तरह "to": equal to, identical to, superior to; पर "different from"।
✖ "from" आरंभ-बिंदु/स्रोत के लिए (from Delhi; different from)। "with" साथ/साधन के लिए (cut with a knife; pleased with)। "as" समानता की तुलना (as ... as) या "क्योंकि" अर्थ में।
N62738.expe:
✔ "similar to" — alike or resembling someone/something. Correct sentence: Asha is similar to her brother in looks.
📌 Similarly with "to": equal to, identical to, superior to; but "different from".
✖ "from" shows origin/source (from Delhi; different from). "with" shows accompaniment/instrument (cut with a knife; pleased with). "as" is used in equal comparison (as ... as) or meaning "because".

N62739.exp:
✔ "Either ... or" युग्मित (correlative) संयोजक है — दोनों में से कोई एक। सही वाक्य: Either Lata or Sanjay will attend the meeting.
📌 Either/or के साथ verb पास वाले subject के अनुसार: Either you or he is right। Neither के साथ nor।
✖ "but" विरोध (contrast) बताता है। "and" दो समान बातों को जोड़ता है (addition)। "nor" केवल neither के साथ या नकारात्मक वाक्य में आता है।
N62739.expe:
✔ "Either ... or" is a correlative pair meaning one of the two. Correct sentence: Either Lata or Sanjay will attend the meeting.
📌 With either/or the verb agrees with the nearer subject: Either you or he is right. Neither goes with nor.
✖ "but" shows contrast. "and" joins similar ideas (addition). "nor" is used with "neither" or after a negative.

N62740.exp:
✔ "whether" संदेह/अनिश्चितता (doubt) बताता है — पता नहीं कि वह मानेगी या नहीं। सही वाक्य: I cannot say whether Anita will agree.
📌 whether के साथ "or not" जोड़ सकते हैं: whether she will agree or not। doubt, know, ask, wonder के बाद प्रायः whether/if।
✖ "lest" = ऐसा न हो कि (lest + should): Work hard lest you should fail। "though" = यद्यपि (विरोध/concession)। "unless" = यदि नहीं (if not)।
N62740.expe:
✔ "whether" expresses doubt/uncertainty — not sure if she will agree. Correct sentence: I cannot say whether Anita will agree.
📌 "or not" can follow: whether she will agree or not. Verbs like doubt, know, ask, wonder are often followed by whether/if.
✖ "lest" means "for fear that" (lest + should): Work hard lest you should fail. "though" means "in spite of the fact that" (concession). "unless" means "if not".

N62741.exp:
✔ सामान्य देशों के नाम (proper noun) से पहले कोई article नहीं लगता — Rahul has gone to Bhutan.
📌 उदाहरण: India, Nepal, Bhutan, Japan। पर the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, the Maldives (United/Kingdom/बहुवचन नाम) के साथ "the"।
✖ "the" देश के नाम के साथ सामान्यतः नहीं लगता। "a" singular countable common noun के लिए है; देश के नाम के साथ नहीं। "an" singular countable common noun के लिए है; देश के नाम के साथ नहीं।
N62741.expe:
✔ Ordinary country names (proper nouns) take no article — Rahul has gone to Bhutan.
📌 Examples: India, Nepal, Bhutan, Japan. But the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, the Maldives (United/Kingdom/plural names) take "the".
✖ "the" is not normally used with a country name. "a" is for a singular countable common noun, not a country name. "an" is for a singular countable common noun, not a country name.

N62742.exp:
✔ "on behalf of" — किसी की ओर से (प्रतिनिधि के रूप में); निश्चित मुहावरा। सही वाक्य: My uncle spoke on behalf of the team.
📌 उदाहरण: The minister spoke on behalf of the government। इसी तरह "in favour of" (पक्ष में)।
✖ "by" साधन/कर्ता या समय-सीमा के लिए (by bus, by Monday)। "for" उद्देश्य या अवधि के लिए (for you, for two hours)। "at" निश्चित समय/बिंदु-स्थान के लिए (at 5 pm, at the gate)।
N62742.expe:
✔ "on behalf of" — as a representative of; a fixed phrase. Correct sentence: My uncle spoke on behalf of the team.
📌 Example: The minister spoke on behalf of the government. Similarly "in favour of" (in support of).
✖ "by" shows means/agent or a deadline (by bus, by Monday). "for" shows purpose or duration (for you, for two hours). "at" is for an exact time or point (at 5 pm, at the gate).

📌 Correlative pairs: either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, whether ... or.

N62745.exp:

N62746.exp:
✔ सही collocation 'apologise for' है। किसी व्यक्ति से (to) किसी गलती के लिए (for) क्षमा माँगी जाती है — apologise for. सही वाक्य: "Radha apologised for the mistake."
📌 इसी तरह: thank for, blame for, punish for.
✖ of — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'jealous of, aware of' में। on — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'rely on, insist on' में। at — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'good at, look at' में।
N62746.expe:
✔ The correct collocation is 'apologise for'. One apologises TO a person FOR a fault. Correct: "Radha apologised for the mistake."
📌 Similar: thank for, blame for, punish for.
✖ of — wrong here; used in e.g. 'jealous of, aware of'. on — wrong here; used in e.g. 'rely on, insist on'. at — wrong here; used in e.g. 'good at, look at'.

N62747.exp:
✔ सही collocation 'prefer ... to' है। 'Prefer' के साथ तुलना में 'than' नहीं, 'to' आता है: prefer A to B. सही वाक्य: "Rohan prefers walking to running."
📌 Latin comparatives भी 'to' लेते हैं: senior to, superior to, inferior to; पर 'would rather ... than'.
✖ over — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'over the wall, control over' में। from — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'suffer from, abstain from' में। than — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'taller than' में।
N62747.expe:
✔ The correct collocation is 'prefer ... to'. 'Prefer' takes 'to' (not 'than') for comparison: prefer A to B. Correct: "Rohan prefers walking to running."
📌 Also 'to': senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to. But 'would rather ... than'.
✖ over — wrong here; used in e.g. 'over the wall, control over'. from — wrong here; used in e.g. 'suffer from, abstain from'. than — wrong here; used in e.g. 'taller than'.

N62748.exp:
✔ 'Till' = जब तक; मेरे लौटने तक यहीं रुको। सही वाक्य: "Wait here till I return."
📌 'Till/until' के बाद negative नहीं आता।
✖ unless — का अर्थ 'यदि नहीं' (शर्त) है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। lest — का अर्थ 'कहीं ऐसा न हो कि' है; इसके बाद 'should' आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। since — कारण या समय-बिंदु ('since Monday') बताता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
N62748.expe:
✔ 'Till' = up to the time when; wait here until I come back. Correct: "Wait here till I return."
📌 'Till/until' is not followed by a negative ('till I return', not 'till I do not return').
✖ unless — means 'if not' (condition); does not fit here. lest — means 'for fear that'; takes 'should' after it; does not fit here. since — shows reason or a point of time ('since Monday'); does not fit here.

N62749.exp:
✔ अधिकांश देशों के नाम (Japan, Nepal, France...) proper noun हैं; इनसे पहले article नहीं लगता। सही वाक्य: "Vikas has gone to Japan."
📌 बहुवचन या Republic/Kingdom/States वाले नामों में 'the': the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, the Maldives।

N62749.expe:

📌 'The' is used with country names that are plural or contain Republic/Kingdom/States: the USA, the UK, the Netherlands, the Maldives.
✖ the — only for names like the USA, the UK, the Netherlands. an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here. a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here.

N62750.exp:
✔ सही collocation 'abstain from' है। 'Abstain' (दूर रहना) के बाद 'from' आता है। सही वाक्य: "Rekha abstains from smoking."
📌 इसी तरह: refrain from, desist from, prevent from.
✖ of — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'jealous of, aware of' में। with — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'agree with (person), cope with' में। to — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'reply to, prefer to' में।

📌 Similar: refrain from, desist from, prevent from.
✖ of — wrong here; used in e.g. 'jealous of, aware of'. with — wrong here; used in e.g. 'agree with (person), cope with'. to — wrong here; used in e.g. 'reply to, prefer to'.

N62751.exp:
✔ Correlative जोड़ा: either ... or (दो में से एक)। सही वाक्य: "Either Sita or Radha will attend the meeting."
📌 जोड़े: neither...nor, both...and, not only...but also; verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार।
✖ and — समान विचारों को जोड़ता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। nor — केवल 'neither' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। but — विरोध (contrast) बताता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
N62751.expe:
✔ Correlative pair: either ... or (choice between two). Correct: "Either Sita or Radha will attend the meeting."

✖ and — joins similar ideas (addition); does not fit here. nor — pairs only with 'neither'; does not fit here. but — shows contrast; does not fit here.

N62752.exp:
✔ दोनों उपवाक्यों में विरोध है (तेज़ दौड़ा फिर भी बस छूटी), इसलिए 'but'। सही वाक्य: "Suresh ran fast but he could not catch the bus."
📌 विरोध-सूचक: but, yet, still, however, although।
✖ because — कारण बताता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। and so — परिणाम बताता है, विरोध नहीं; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। so — परिणाम बताता है, विरोध नहीं; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
N62752.expe:
✔ Two clauses show contrast (ran fast — yet missed the bus), so 'but' is used. Correct: "Suresh ran fast but he could not catch the bus."
📌 Contrast linkers: but, yet, still, however, although.
✖ because — gives a reason; does not fit here. and so — shows result, not contrast; does not fit here. so — shows result, not contrast; does not fit here.

N62753.exp:

✖ an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here. a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here. the — only in 'the ... language' or for a people (the English).

N62756.exp:
✔ 'So that' उद्देश्य बताता है: धीरे बोले ताकि सब समझ सकें। सही वाक्य: "My uncle spoke slowly so that everyone could understand."

N62757.exp:

✖ a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here. no article — an article is required here. an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here.

✖ at — wrong here; used in e.g. 'good at, look at'. for — wrong here; used in e.g. 'famous for, eligible for'. to — wrong here; used in e.g. 'reply to, prefer to'.

✔ The correct collocation is 'abstain from'. 'Abstain' (keep oneself away) is followed by 'from'. Correct: "My uncle abstains from smoking."
📌 Similar: refrain from, desist from, prevent from.
✖ with — wrong here; used in e.g. 'agree with (person), cope with'. of — wrong here; used in e.g. 'jealous of, aware of'. to — wrong here; used in e.g. 'reply to, prefer to'.

N62781.exp:
✔ Correlative जोड़ा: both ... and; verb plural (are) होती है। सही वाक्य: "Both Vikas and Meena are teachers."
📌 'Both...as well as' गलत है। अन्य: either...or, neither...nor।
✖ nor — केवल 'neither' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। or — 'either' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। as well as — 'both ... as well as' गलत है; 'both' का जोड़ा 'and' है।
N62781.expe:
✔ Correlative pair: both ... and; the verb is plural (are). Correct: "Both Vikas and Meena are teachers."
📌 'Both...as well as' is wrong. Other pairs: either...or, neither...nor.
✖ nor — pairs only with 'neither'; does not fit here. or — pairs with 'either'; does not fit here. as well as — 'both ... as well as' is incorrect; 'both' pairs with 'and'.

N62782.exp:
✔ भाषाओं के नाम से पहले article नहीं: speak Hindi/English। सही वाक्य: "My brother speaks Hindi fluently."
📌 'language' शब्द साथ हो तो 'the' (the Hindi language); लोगों के लिए 'the English'।
✖ the — केवल 'the ... language' या लोगों (the English) के लिए। an — स्वर ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। a — व्यंजन ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं।
N62782.expe:
✔ Names of languages take no article: speak Hindi/English/Sanskrit. Correct: "My brother speaks Hindi fluently."
📌 'The' is used when 'language' follows (the Hindi language) or for the people (the English = English people).
✖ the — only in 'the ... language' or for a people (the English). an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here. a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here.

N62783.exp:
✔ सही collocation 'believe in' है। किसी सिद्धांत/मूल्य में आस्था के लिए 'believe in' आता है। सही वाक्य: "Priya believes in hard work."
📌 किसी की बात सच मानने पर 'believe someone' (बिना preposition)।
✖ with — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'agree with (person), cope with' में। on — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'rely on, insist on' में। at — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'good at, look at' में।
N62783.expe:
✔ The correct collocation is 'believe in'. 'Believe in' = have faith in an idea or value (hard work). Correct: "Priya believes in hard work."
📌 'Believe someone' = accept what a person says (no preposition).
✖ with — wrong here; used in e.g. 'agree with (person), cope with'. on — wrong here; used in e.g. 'rely on, insist on'. at — wrong here; used in e.g. 'good at, look at'.

N62784.exp:
✔ Correlative जोड़ा: neither ... nor (न यह, न वह)। सही वाक्य: "Neither Meena nor Jyoti came to the party."
📌 जोड़े: either...or, both...and, not only...but also।
✖ but — विरोध (contrast) बताता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। and — समान विचारों को जोड़ता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं। or — 'either' के साथ आता है; यहाँ उपयुक्त नहीं।
N62784.expe:
✔ Correlative pair: neither ... nor (not one and not the other). Correct: "Neither Meena nor Jyoti came to the party."
📌 Pairs: either...or, both...and, not only...but also.
✖ but — shows contrast; does not fit here. and — joins similar ideas (addition); does not fit here. or — pairs with 'either'; does not fit here.

N62785.exp:
✔ खेलों के नाम से पहले article नहीं: play football, tennis। सही वाक्य: "Arjun plays football every evening."
📌 किंतु वाद्य यंत्रों के साथ 'the': play the guitar, play the flute।
✖ the — वाद्य यंत्रों के साथ, खेलों के साथ नहीं। a — व्यंजन ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं। an — स्वर ध्वनि वाले एकवचन countable noun से पहले; यहाँ नहीं।
N62785.expe:
✔ Names of games/sports take no article: play football, tennis, volleyball. Correct: "Arjun plays football every evening."
📌 But musical instruments take 'the': play the guitar, play the flute.
✖ the — used with musical instruments, not games. a — used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound; not here. an — used before a vowel sound in a singular countable noun; not here.

N62786.exp:
✔ सही collocation 'in charge of' है। Fixed phrase 'in charge of' = किसी का प्रभारी होना। सही वाक्य: "Pooja is in charge of the office."
📌 इसी तरह: in favour of, in spite of, in place of.
✖ on — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'rely on, insist on' में। with — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'agree with (person), cope with' में। for — यहाँ गलत; इसका प्रयोग जैसे 'famous for, eligible for' में।
N62786.expe:
✔ The correct collocation is 'in charge of'. Fixed phrase: 'in charge of' = responsible for managing. Correct: "Pooja is in charge of the office."
📌 Similar phrases: in favour of, in spite of, in place of.
✖ on — wrong here; used in e.g. 'rely on, insist on'. with — wrong here; used in e.g. 'agree with (person), cope with'. for — wrong here; used in e.g. 'famous for, eligible for'.
